title.official: Attorney General’s right to be heard

subdivision.heading: Additional Rules Specific to Originating Applications for Judicial Review

operative_text.controlling:
3.17   The Minister of Justice or the Attorney General for Canada,
or both, as the case requires, is entitled as of right to be heard on an
originating application for judicial review.

BOOK_A.commentary:
*6 Information Note The Court may grant intervenor status to other persons under rule 2.10 [Intervenor status]. Defined Terms Minister of Justice and Attorney General

Related Provisions 2.10 (intervenor status) See also note G to R.3.15,supra, and R.3.16n.On intervention by the Attorney General, see theAuercase. Where an Act requires notice to the two Attorneys General of a constitutional question in other

types of litigation, whether failure to give the notice is fatal and the remedy is just an adjournment is disputed? But appeal courts often refuse to hear such unnotified questions. 1Trang v.R. (Alta.)2014 ABCA 382, 588 AR 13. 2Trang v.R.,supra. 3E.G.v.Correctional Service of Can. (#2)2015 ABQB 539, [2015] AJ #929 (Aug 28).

4R.P. v.Dir. of Child,Youth & Fam.Enhancement2018 ABQB 391, JCE 1803 07821 (May 15) (¶'s 15-18). 5R.P. v.Dir. of Child,etc.,supra(¶'s 19-23). 6Quite similar to previous 1987 R.753.10(2), new in 1987.

1Normally an affidavit from the Attorney General explaining the effect of the case on the government, or its special expertise, is very desirable, but here the effect on both governments was pretty clear, and the other Attorney General had filed such an affidavit:Edm. Policy Service v. Info. & Privacy Comm'r.,infra. 2Edm.Police Service v.Info.& Privacy Comm'r.2021 ABCA 428, 35 Alta LR(7th) 109 (one JA) (¶'s 6-21). 3Quite similar to previous 1987 R.753.12 and 1968 R.743(2), new then. 4IMS Health Can.v.Info.& Privacy Comm'r.2005 ABCA 325, 376 AR 336.But cf.Robertsonv.Wasylyshen

*(Edm.Police Service) (#9)2004 ABQB 243, 355 AR 281.It is up to the Attorney General whether and when to intervene in an appeal. TheAttorney General is the government's official legal adviser.The history of that officer representing the Crown is well over 500 years old.

BOOK_A.commentary_review_flag: Read in full, p.3-57 (line 1521) to p.3-58 (line 1537): rule text, Information Note, Defined Terms, Related Provisions, a note of two paragraphs and footnotes as printed; the built commentary ends with the title of 3.18 ('Notice to Obtain Record of Proceedings', line 1539). (1) Information Note (p.3-57, line 1522): 'The Court may grant intervenor status to other persons under rule 2.10 [Intervenor status].' - the same words as Book C's information note; the official 3.17 has no information note in the text searched (official lines 4141-4145), and official 2.10 is titled 'Intervenor status' (title matches). Book A's copy is inside the commentary text (not split out), so the built information-note record shows Book C only. (2) Defined Terms 'Minister of Justice and Attorney General': the official Appendix has 'Minister' (= the Minister of Justice for Alberta) and no such term; official 3.17 reads 'The Minister of Justice or the Attorney General for Canada, or both' (same point as in the 3.15 flag). (3) Related Provisions '2.10 (intervenor status)': matches the official title. (4) Pointers: 'See also note G to R.3.15, supra' lands (3.15 note G Service and Parties); 'R.3.16n.' has no visible target about the Attorney General (see the 3.16 see_also); 'On intervention by the Attorney General, see the Auer case' points to footnote 7, Auer v. Auer 2018 ABQB 510, [2018] 9 WWR 744, printed at the top of p.3-57 (line 1509) inside the built 3.16 commentary together with footnote 8 ('not fatal: J.F.M. v. V.P. (#3) 2003 ABQB 982; Fatal: Sedgwick v. Edm. Real Est. Bd. etc. 2021 ABQB 59; Golden Pinnacle Consultants v. Dir. of Fair Trading 2023 ABKB 81'), and the end of this note's sentence about failure to give notice ('successfully appeal on that ground?', line 1506): those pieces are 3.17's. Footnotes 1-5 on p.3-57 (Trang, E.G., R.P.) precede footnote 6 (this rule's history) and belong to 3.16's note. (5) The note says 'Where an Act requires notice to the two Attorneys General of a constitutional question in other types of litigation, whether failure to give the notice is fatal and the remedy is just an adjournment is disputed': the Act is not named and is outside the Rules; not checked. p.3-58 footnotes: fn 1-2 (affidavit from the Attorney General; Edm. Police Service v. Info. & Privacy Comm'r. 2021 ABCA 428) and fn 4 (IMS Health Can. v. Info. & Privacy Comm'r. 2005 ABCA 325; cf. Robertson v. Wasylyshen (#9) 2004 ABQB 243) go with this note's sentence 'It is up to the Attorney General whether and when to intervene in an appeal' (fn 4 could belong to the 3.18 text that precedes it on the page: not shown); fn 3 ('Quite similar to previous 1987 R.753.12 and 1968 R.743(2), new then') is the history of 3.18 (official 3.18 is the notice to send up the record; Book B's Brewer quotation names 'Rr. 753.12 and 753.13' as the old record rules). (6) Book A rule 2.10's related provision (combined_rule2.txt p.2-22, line 1026) '3.17 (standing of Attorney General on judicial review)' describes 3.17 as 'standing'; the official title and text are the Attorney General's right to be heard. (7) Case law and the 500-year history sentence were not checked.
